# Attention Is All You Need: Summary

## Research background

Sequence transduction was dominated by recurrent or convolutional encoder–decoder models; the strongest systems also linked encoder and decoder with attention. [Abstract: dominant RNN/CNN encoder–decoder setup](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-300178317a9be800) RNNs such as LSTM and gated recurrent networks were the established state of the art for language modeling and machine translation, [Introduction: RNN/LSTM as prior SOTA](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-1732a5a95131e0e4) but their step-by-step dependence of ht on ht−1 blocks parallelization within an example and remains a bottleneck at long lengths. [Introduction: sequential computation constraint](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-76d1bf6ff31894e4) Attention already modeled distance-independent dependencies, yet was almost always paired with recurrence. [Introduction: attention used with RNNs](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-9276c814498525c3) CNN alternatives (Extended Neural GPU, ByteNet, ConvS2S) parallelize over positions, but the cost of relating distant positions still grows with distance—linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet—making long-range learning harder. [Background: CNN path-length growth](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-3a26294661233ea4) Against that backdrop, the authors present the Transformer as the first transduction model that computes input and output representations entirely with self-attention, without sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution. [Background: first fully self-attentive transduction model](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-1b307781c1a10337)

## Core contributions

1. **Transformer architecture**
   A simple network based solely on attention, removing recurrence and convolutions while keeping an encoder–decoder layout: the encoder maps (x1,…,xn) to continuous z, and the decoder auto-regressively emits (y1,…,ym). [Abstract: propose Transformer](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-300178317a9be800) [Introduction: attention-only global dependencies](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-60aecf560cb69ae7) [Model Architecture: encoder–decoder mapping](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-295098973fae1c81) [Model Architecture: stacked self-attention and FFN](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-948d34e9033c9b71)

2. **Encoder and decoder stacks**
   Both use N=6 identical layers with residual connections and LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)), and d_model=512. Each encoder layer has multi-head self-attention plus a position-wise feed-forward network; each decoder layer adds encoder–decoder multi-head attention and masks self-attention so position i depends only on outputs before i. [Encoder stack: N=6, residuals, d_model=512](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-18350fa39bdabdbc) [Decoder stack: third attention sub-layer and masking](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-be9344d005fb75ba)

3. **Scaled Dot-Product Attention**
   With queries/keys of dimension dk and values of dimension dv, Attention(Q,K,V)=softmax(QK^T/√dk)V; dividing by √dk offsets large-magnitude products when dk is large. [Scaled Dot-Product Attention definition](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-e870cebf3b1ed063) [Equation 1: Attention(Q,K,V)](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-abf10228ac7062a8) [Scaling by 1/√dk for large dk](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-d517b063a784e48e)

4. **Multi-Head Attention and its three uses**
   Queries, keys, and values are projected h times; heads run in parallel, then concatenate and project. The paper uses h=8 with dk=dv=d_model/h=64 so total cost stays near single-head full-width attention, letting the model attend different subspaces at once. [Multi-head projection design](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-8f309afc5b6f0964) [MultiHead formula](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-314c2a183be84fdb) [h=8, dk=dv=64](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-5a67a027ea5b3614) [Joint attention across subspaces](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-c8532a407fc71b41) The same mechanism appears as encoder–decoder attention, encoder self-attention, and masked decoder self-attention. [Encoder–decoder attention](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-a294838979158a20) [Encoder self-attention](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-21ac1f34ab6caa7b) [Masked decoder self-attention](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-0461439223cb3ce6)

5. **Position-wise FFN and sinusoidal positional encoding**
   Each layer applies FFN(x)=max(0,xW1+b1)W2+b2 with d_model=512 and d_ff=2048. [Position-wise FFN description](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-e310e894e5611826) [Equation 2: FFN](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-5c327aed3ebd032f) [d_model=512, d_ff=2048](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-1a272a6814e47fd7) Without recurrence or convolution, order is injected by sinusoidal PE(pos,2i)=sin(pos/10000^{2i/d_model}) and PE(pos,2i+1)=cos(pos/10000^{2i/d_model}); learned embeddings matched quality, but sinusoids were kept for possible length extrapolation. [Need for positional encodings](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-64ff1393f82c4c68) [Sinusoidal PE formulas](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-b7b475fc636bc084) [Sinusoidal vs learned PE](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-703be9a227e3bbc9)

6. **Why self-attention**
   Relative to recurrence and convolution, self-attention connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations (vs O(n) for RNNs), shortens maximum path length for long-range dependencies, and is computationally favorable when sequence length n is smaller than representation dimension d. [Complexity and parallelization desiderata](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-b95168e0a41f1b71) [Path-length motivation](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-ace193f98745a722) [Self-attention vs RNN sequential cost](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-9815228a51361c83) [Table 1: path length and complexity](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-d1b71be345c11a4d)

## Experimental results

1. **WMT 2014 English→German — BLEU 28.4**
   Transformer (big) sets a new state-of-the-art BLEU of 28.4, exceeding the best prior models including ensembles by more than 2.0 BLEU after 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs; even the base model beats prior published models and ensembles at a fraction of their training cost. [En–De results: BLEU 28.4](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-a48a937a4ad7552e) [Table 2 caption: BLEU and training cost](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-49d5c3c0bbdbf347)

2. **WMT 2014 English→French — BLEU 41.0**
   The big model reaches BLEU 41.0, outperforming all previously published single models at less than one-fourth the training cost of the prior state of the art (this En–Fr big run used P_drop=0.1 instead of 0.3). [En–Fr results: BLEU 41.0](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-60954fb1a674ba15) [Table 2: translation cost comparison](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-49d5c3c0bbdbf347)

3. **Training data and schedule**
   En–De uses about 4.5M sentence pairs (BPE, ~37K shared vocabulary); En–Fr uses 36M sentences (32K word-piece vocabulary); batches hold about 25K source and 25K target tokens. Base models train for 100,000 steps (~12 hours) and big models for 300,000 steps (3.5 days) on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. [Training data and batching](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-58f23864152069a2) [Hardware and training schedule](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-aaa1688fd0ea5e8f)

4. **Architecture ablations (Table 3, newstest2013)**
   On English→German development, single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting and quality also falls with too many heads; shrinking key size dk hurts quality; larger models help and dropout reduces overfitting; learned positional embeddings match sinusoidal encodings closely. [Ablation protocol on newstest2013](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-5c19bc6bac0d3a9a) [Head-count ablation: −0.9 BLEU for single head](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-2c5acb64be0e2502) [dk, model size, dropout, PE ablations](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-1730fe96b3377c5d) [Table 3 caption: architecture variations](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-23cca5667197529d)

5. **English constituency parsing**
   A 4-layer Transformer with d_model=1024 trained on WSJ (~40K sentences) and a semi-supervised corpus (~17M sentences) generalizes well: Table 4 results beat all prior reported models except Recurrent Neural Network Grammar, and—unlike earlier RNN sequence-to-sequence systems—the Transformer outperforms BerkeleyParser even with only the 40K WSJ training set. [Parsing task motivation](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-323c610c0c87af92) [Parsing training setups](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-eeea060215ffcde1) [Table 4: parsing vs prior models](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-9ad73223b3bcd390) [WSJ-only vs BerkeleyParser](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-4aca42887fd919dc) [Table 4 caption: WSJ Section 23](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-3785b8ec731e72bb)

## Main conclusions

The work introduces the Transformer as the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing recurrent encoder–decoder layers with multi-headed self-attention. [Conclusion: attention-only transduction model](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-ed3351916654be2a) On translation it trains substantially faster than recurrent or convolutional architectures and reaches a new state of the art on WMT 2014 English→German and English→French; on English→German the best model also surpasses all previously reported ensembles. [Conclusion: faster training and SOTA translation](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-f2f50ad1f79a767b) The authors plan to extend attention-based models to other tasks and non-text modalities, study local/restricted attention for large inputs such as images, audio, and video, and pursue less sequential generation. [Conclusion: future work directions](thinkreader://paper/paper-a89f51c3ffa647c7?evidence=ev-7ebb4179a36f948d)
